subject: Scaling constraints and next steps for Luminex inference topology
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@luminex.ai>, Samuel Lee <samuel@luminex.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Scaling constraints and next steps for Luminex inference topology

Hi Anna / Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick write-up to capture the pain, goals, and the architectural options we discussed so the team has a single source of truth. I pulled the three top items we heard on the call and outlined a proposed skeleton topology.

Key pain points (as we heard):
- Bursty customer traffic with tight 95th pct latency targets for chat (~200–250ms p95) during peak shopping windows.
- Current on-prem stack can’t sustain consistent KV-cache-backed sessions at 100–150 RPS without either huge memory overhead or unacceptably high tail latency.
- Procurement and security team require audit logs and KMS integration for any private deployment.

Goals / success criteria:
- p95 generation latency <= 250ms for short (<=128 token) convo turns at 100 RPS baseline; degrade gracefully during bursts via fallback model.
- End-to-end throughput to support 10k active sessions with prefix caching and per-tenant routing.
- Data residency in us-west and auditability (access logs retained 90 days).

Model & runtime constraints we discussed:
- Primary model: ~13B dense / quantized variant (FP16->4-bit opted) for production traffic.
- Fallback: smaller 6–7B low-cost variant for degraded mode to protect latency SLOs.
- Requires KV cache retention per session + prefix caching (cache hit rate goal 60–70% for repeat flows).

Suggested topology (high level):
- Dedicated pool in us-west (G4/GA-type fleet equivalent) with autoscale based on queue depth + predictive burst buffer.
- Edge routing: route short requests to low-latency warm pool; larger or long-context requests to a scaled burst cluster.
- Multi-tier model variants pinned per route for graceful fallback; automatic circuit-breaker if GPU queueing exceeds threshold.

Attached: redwood_topology_proposal.pdf (sketch + sizing), luminex_kpi_snapshot.xlsx you shared, perf-harness-instructions.txt (how we’ll run perf tests).

Next steps (proposed owner / ETA):
- Rafael: share topology pdf + test harness by EOD today (attached).
- Luminex infra: confirm data residency & KMS requirements by Wednesday 2028-04-18 (Anna).
- Redwood infra: run a micro-benchmark (13B quantized) against your sample traffic pattern — target results by 2028-04-20.
- Procurement: procurement team to share any standard contract redlines by 2028-04-25.

If that matches your read, I’ll schedule a 45-min deep-dive w/ infra + SRE for Wednesday next week to review sizing and the perf plan.

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): redwood_topology_proposal.pdf (PDF), luminex_kpi_snapshot.xlsx (Excel), perf-harness-instructions.txt (Text)

To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Lee <samuel@luminex.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scaling constraints and next steps for Luminex inference topology

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates:
- Data residency: the primary requirement is US-West for inference and logs must remain in our VPC. Are you proposing an on-prem appliance or a VPC-private Redwood Private deployment?
- Audit logs / KMS: we need HSM-backed key management (customer-controlled) and an audit trail for all model access. Can you confirm Redwood supports a customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private mode?
- Procurement: rough timeline looks like 2–3 weeks for an initial term sheet; we’ll aim to share redlines by 2028-04-25 but procurement might push if legal requires more detail.

If those are doable, the perf window and canary timeline you suggested make sense. Please also include a minimal list of telemetry events we’ll get out-of-box for the first canary.

Best,
Anna Park
Head of Product Ops | Luminex Systems
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Anna Park <anna@luminex.ai>
Date: 2028-04-16T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scaling constraints and next steps for Luminex inference topology

Rafael / Anna —

Quick tech note from our infra side after reviewing the PDF + KPIs:
- Perf target mapping: to hit 250ms p95 at 100 RPS for 13B quantized we estimate ~6–8 GPUs in a warm pool with aggressive KV cache warming. We’ll validate with a perf run.
- Burst plan: add a cold burst lane that can spin up another 8–12 GPUs; however, tail latency will likely increase if we rely solely on cold starts — hence the fallback model is critical.
- KV cache sizing: based on sample traffic the working set should fit within ~120–160GB of fast-memory across the warm pool (we’ll provide a concrete allocation matrix).

Action items I’ll own:
- Provide a bench script + SLO assertion harness (see perf-harness-instructions.txt) by 2028-04-17.
- Draft a recommended autoscale policy for warm vs. burst lanes and share a CPU/GPU cost delta table for Luminex’s review by 2028-04-18.

Note for procurement/legal: we support customer-managed KMS in Private mode and can produce audit logs with 1s granularity; will surface the retention/format details in the runbook.

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@luminex.ai>, Samuel Lee <samuel@luminex.ai>, Procurement <procurement@luminex.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scaling constraints and next steps for Luminex inference topology

Anna / Sam / Procurement —

Following internal alignment and Karthik’s notes, quick update and confirmed dates:
- Redwood confirms Private deployment option with customer-managed KMS/HSM and 1s-granularity audit logs. We’ll include retention/format detail in the runbook. (Karthik will attach the runbook draft in the next message.)
- Perf run: Redwood will execute the 13B quantized micro-benchmark against the sample traces. Target delivery: 2028-04-20. Rafael will share test results + raw logs.
- Procurement: expect a term sheet by 2028-04-25; if legal requires an NDA addendum for HSM proofs we can get that in 3 business days once requested.
- Canary: propose May 5–7 for a limited canary (5% traffic) if perf looks good. Full roll by May 20 contingent on SLA acceptance.

Please reply with any conflicts. If no objections I’ll lock the deep-dive on 2028-04-19 10:30am PT (45m) to walk through the autoscale policy, KV sizing, and canary checklist.

Cheers,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
